lead: Thursday's lead was legal: [a US appeals court upheld the supply-chain-risk designation on Anthropic](../summaries/a3a5741553cc.md). [Google's Project Suncatcher took ML infrastructure to space](../summaries/a1a9cda1ffd3.md), [Microsoft abandoned the personal chatbot race with a Copilot reboot](../summaries/b20df8221f7f.md), and [a teardown suggested Meta's Muse runs an OpenAI model labeled muse-special](../summaries/b91562b4ca5c.md). [Classified estimates put NSA model-testing spend in the billions](../summaries/9b09b8c1bdb4.md).

sections.title: Anthropic designated a supply-chain risk
sections.intro: The appeals court's upheld designation was the day's most-read story - and a first-of-its-kind constraint on a frontier lab.

sections.title: Corporate strategy shifts
sections.intro: Microsoft's Copilot reboot, Muse's borrowed model, Anthropic's Palantir-style governance ask, and an $11.6B Akamai commitment.

sections.title: The state and the models
sections.intro: NSA testing billions, Xi and Trump at a summit, Chinese subsidies, and AI deciding who gets medical care.

sections.title: Niche science and strange side-effects
sections.intro: LLMs decoding 17th-century alchemical letters, nine-loop amplitudes, ML in orbit, and Japanese used-book stores booming on AI-driven bulk buying.

sections.title: Agent tooling matures
sections.intro: Automatic project memory for Claude Code, Docker's cloud sandboxes, an agentic CUDA optimizer, code review by the writing agent, and Gemini Live avatars.

sections.title: Society edges
sections.intro: A tutoring company telling parents to use AI instead, Snowden on AI surveillance, a game wiki DDoSed after an AI ban, and 'don't let AI kill the author'.
